preconditions.description: The number of vertices in the logical scheme is between 2 and 1,000,000 inclusive.
Each vertex description line has exactly three space-separated tokens: type, followed by input indices (1 or 2 for non-IN types).

preconditions.expression: all(line.split()[0] in ['AND', 'OR', 'XOR', 'NOT', 'IN'] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each vertex type is one of 'AND', 'OR', 'XOR', 'NOT', or 'IN'.

preconditions.expression: all(int(line.split()[1]) in range(1, n+1) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: All input indices in vertex descriptions are valid vertex indices (1 to n).

preconditions.expression: all(int(line.split()[1]) != 1 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.split()[0] == 'IN')
preconditions.description: The root vertex (1) is not an input (i.e., it is not of type 'IN').

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 3 and line.split()[0] in ['AND', 'OR', 'XOR'] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if int(line.split()[1]) == 1)
preconditions.description: The root vertex (1) is a logical element with exactly two inputs (AND, OR, or XOR).

preconditions.expression: all(int(line.split()[1]) != int(line.split()[2]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.split()[0] in ['AND', 'OR', 'XOR'])
preconditions.description: For AND, OR, and XOR gates, the two input indices are distinct.

preconditions.expression: all(int(line.split()[1]) != int(line.split()[2]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.split()[0] == 'NOT')
preconditions.description: For NOT gates, the single input index is valid (redundant with P4, but explicit).

preconditions.expression: all(int(line.split()[2]) == 0 or int(line.split()[2]) == 1 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] if line.split()[0] == 'IN')
preconditions.description: Each input vertex ('IN') has a value of 0 or 1.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout) == len([i for i in range(1, n+1) if stdin.splitlines()[i].split()[0] == 'IN'])
postconditions.description: The output string has one character for each input vertex in ascending order of their indices.

postconditions.expression: all(c in ['0', '1'] for c in stdout)
postconditions.description: Each character in the output string is either '0' or '1'.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout[i] == str(original_output ^ (1 if original_input[i] == 0 else 0)) for i in range(len(stdout)))
postconditions.description: For each input vertex i (in ascending order), the output character is the result of flipping the original input value of i and computing the new output of the scheme. Here, original_output is the output of the scheme with original inputs, and original_input[i] is the original value of input i.
